messages:
eric: quick heads-up — I hit a repeatable KV paging/eviction pattern on long-context Mistral runs (50k+ tokens). looks like interleaved slab allocations + rope scaling cause periodic full-scan evicts :confused:

maya: can you paste the minimal repro? is this only Mistral or also Qwen/LLama variants?

eric: repro attached in the thread (quick steps):
1) start a persistent session pinned to mistral-7b with MQA enabled
2) send a long expanding prompt that triggers rope scaling (we use +2048 every 4k tokens)
3) tail the runtime alloc log and watch KV page churn

sofia: interesting — we saw something sort of like this but that was Qwen-specific and tied to GQA->MQA switchover. do you have profiler snippets?

eric: here's the relevant lines from kv-alloc.log (trimmed):
```
2026-10-05T12:02:11Z alloc slab 0x7f3a size 1.2MB model=Mistral-7B kernel=opt_v1
2026-10-05T12:02:12Z page commit idx=1024 slab=0x7f3a seq=4096
2026-10-05T12:02:13Z evict page idx=512 reason=slot_reuse_fail
2026-10-05T12:02:13Z gc sweep start
2026-10-05T12:02:14Z page commit idx=1536 slab=0x7f3a seq=6144
2026-10-05T12:02:15Z evict page idx=1024 reason=pin_conflict
```
Looks like we allocate new pages while old pages still pinned by prefetch windows — causes a cascade.

maya: does the kernel selection path differ when rope length increases? sometimes we fallback from opt_v1 to opt_v1_mqa when sequence boundary crosses thresholds. could be a kernel mismatch leading to different page stride sizes.

eric: yes — runtime logs show kernel switch at seq=4096: `kernel_select: opt_v1 -> opt_v1_mqa (stride change 64->48)`

sofia: stride change from GQA/MQA mismatch would change per-token KV size; if the allocator expects fixed stride per session it can fragment slabs. any metric for fragmentation?

eric: we ran slab-heatmap over 2h and observed fragmentation score spike after rope-scaling kicks in. snippet: `frag_idx=0.42 -> 0.78` within 3k tokens. Also observed tailing resident set growth even after evicts: `rss +120MB` over 10k tokens.

maya: hmm. two hypotheses: (A) kernel switch changes per-key byte layout and we don't compact in-place -> orphaned partial pages, (B) eviction policy is LRU-ish and gets confused by interleaved MRU pattern from batching heuristics.

sofia: in our Qwen/GQA case it was (A) — we found orphan pages because page signatures included kernel layout version. if layout changes mid-session the old pages become incompatible and can't be reused, so they linger until GC.

eric: repro confirms partial incompat: `page_sig v1 != v2` printed right before a GC pass. But GC only reclaims when fragmentation crosses threshold, so there is a window of growth.

maya: can we force a compact on kernel switch? add a lite compaction that rewrites live KV into new-format pages on the fly. cost vs benefit?

sofia: compaction during warmup could spike latency. alternative: maintain per-slab layout tag and allow mixed layouts with a compatibility shim that translates old-layout pages on first access (pay once). translation cost might be less than full compaction.

eric: translation shim idea is promising. quick micro-bench: translating an old page costs ~200us (one-off) vs compacting slab ~40ms. tradeoff seems favorable for user-visible latency.

maya: another angle — batching heuristics. when we continuous-batch requests with variable sequences, the runtime interleaves long and short contexts causing pinned ranges to overlap. small change: prefer co-batching by sequence length when a session has active rope scaling. i.e., avoid placing long-growth sessions in mixed batches.

eric: I measured batch-cohesion change: co-batching by seq reduces concurrent pinned pages by ~30% in that workload. combined with translation shim, memory growth goes away.

sofia: what about MQA vs GQA tokenization effects — does tokenizer chunking create aligned stride differences across sessions? Qwen's tokenizer produces more mixed-length tokens which might exacerbate fragmentation when combined with batching.

eric: yes on Qwen test we see more frequent kernel toggles because we decide layout by per-request max_seq. Qwen's variance triggers toggles often. Mistral and Llama are more stable.

maya: action items: 
- eric: open a small CL implementing page-layout versioning + translation shim (low-risk) — include unit test that simulates mid-session kernel switch
- sofia: prototype a batch-cohesion scheduler flag and run longseq perf job in staging (scale=50)
- infra-bot: schedule a 6hr long-run on mistral-7b with rope increments to 50k tokens, enable verbose kv logging

infra-bot: scheduled: longrun-mistral-7b-20261005-18:00Z (6h). job id j-8249. will post artifacts to gs://redwood-dev/kvruns/j-8249/

eric: I'll also add an assert to avoid kernel switch if the session has pinned pages > X (safety throttle) — low-risk guard.

sofia: thanks. if we get translation shim + batch cohesion we should cover both root causes. also keep an eye on eviction heuristics: when pinned window is large we could favor evicting oldest full pages instead of partially used ones to reduce fragmentation.

maya: agreed. let's sync tomorrow 10am PT to review traces. thanks all :thumbsup:
